zadanie: A 10-by-12-inch page has margins of 1.5 inches on all sides. What fraction of the area of the page is taken up by the margins? Express your answer as a common fraction.
oczekiwana_odpowiedz: A 10-by-12-inch paper will have an area of $10 \cdot 12 = 120$ square inches. If that paper has 1.5 inch margins on all sides, then the portion of the paper that is not covered by margins will be a rectangular section with length $12 - 2(1.5) = 9$ inches and width $10 - 2(1.5) = 7$ inches. Thus, $9 \cdot 7 = 63$ square inches of the paper will not be taken up by the margins. Since the paper has a total area of $120$ square in, this means that $120-63=57$ square inches of the page is taken up by margins. Thus, margins take up $\dfrac{57}{120}=\boxed{\dfrac{19}{40}}$ of the page.

A 10-by-12-inch page has margins of 1.5 inches on all sides. What fraction of the area of the page is taken up by the margins? Express your answer as a common fraction.
[AI]:
To find the fraction of the area of the page taken up by the margins, we need to calculate the total area of the page and the area of the inner part (the text area), then find the difference.

**Step 1: Calculate the total area of the page.**
The dimensions of the page are 10 inches by 12 inches.
$$\text{Total Area} = \text{width} \times \text{height} = 10 \times 12 = 120 \text{ square inches.}$$

**Step 2: Calculate the dimensions of the inner area.**
The margins are 1.5 inches on all sides. This means we must subtract 1.5 inches from both the left and right sides (for the width) and 1.5 inches from both the top and bottom sides (for the height).
$$\text{Inner Width} = 10 - (1.5 + 1.5) = 10 - 3 = 7 \text{ inches.}$$
$$\text{Inner Height} = 12 - (1.5 + 1.5) = 12 - 3 = 9 \text{ inches.}$$

**Step 3: Calculate the area of the inner part.**
$$\text{Inner Area} = 7 \times 9 = 63 \text{ square inches.}$$

**Step 4: Calculate the area taken up by the margins.**
The area of the margins is the total area minus the inner area.
$$\text{Margin Area} = \text{Total Area} - \text{Inner Area} = 120 - 63 = 57 \text{ square inches.}$$

**Step 5: Calculate the fraction of the total area taken up by the margins.**
The fraction is the margin area divided by the total area.
$$\text{Fraction} = \frac{\text{Margin Area}}{\text{Total Area}} = \frac{57}{120}$$

**Step 6: Simplify the fraction.**
Both 57 and 120 are divisible by 3.
$$57 \div 3 = 19$$
$$120 \div 3 = 40$$
So, the simplified fraction is $\frac{19}{40}$.

The fraction of the area of the page taken up by the margins is $\frac{19}{40}$.

\boxed{\frac{19}{40}}
